_comment: The six clans (Rod), picked when joining a world (PLAN.md §9). `effects` join the player's research bonuses (same keys as research.json, plus researchTime, fortCost, coldDefense against the North front, ambush on field ambushes and trainTime.<unit>); a negative value is a weakness. `unique` names the clan's own unit (units.json) or building (buildings.json), which carries `clan`.

jelen.name: Rod Jelena
jelen.story: The stag-folk of the river meadows: first to sow, first to harvest, their villages grow like spring grass. They were never riders.
jelen.arms: Its arms are those of Nizhny Novgorod (1781): a red stag walking, on silver.

rys.name: Rod Rysa
rys.story: The lynx-folk of the deep woods strike from the shadows of the trees and are gone before the horde can turn. Their elders trust old ways over new learning.
rys.arms: Its arms are those of Gomel (granted in 1781): a gold lynx lying, on blue.

medved.name: Rod Medvěda
medved.story: The bear-folk of the iron hills dig deep and build thick walls. They are slow to leave the den they have made.
medved.arms: Its arms are those of Yaroslavl (1672): a black bear upright with a gold poleaxe, on silver.

bobr.name: Rod Bobra
bobr.story: The beaver-folk know every river and ford; their barges carry what the roads cannot. Their homes are built for trade, not for siege.
bobr.arms: Its arms are those of Bobrov (1781): a beaver in its own colour, on silver.

sokol.name: Rod Sokola
sokol.story: The falcon-folk of the open steppe ride fast and see far; their scouts come home when others do not. They have little patience for stonework.
sokol.arms: Its arms are those of Sokołów Podlaski (seal of 1764): a falcon on an oak branch with a gold ring in its beak, on gold.

volk.name: Rod Volka
volk.story: The wolf-folk of the northern stone fields know the cold and the things that come out of it. Their thin soil feeds them poorly.
volk.arms: Its arms are those of Vovchansk (1781): a silver wolf running over green ground, on blue.
volk.best: Stone and cold resistance (against the North)
